doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

chapter: College, State Department tour and Vienna
title: Vienna jazz competition and meeting a generation of young musicians
summary: After the tour he went to Vienna's 1966 competition, met Mraz, Vitous, Hammer and others, then moved to New York and found work with Mel Lewis.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It’s interesting that you’ve spent some significant time in Europe and in fact very recently is that correct?

Well ever since then because that summer I ended up spending the whole summer in Europe. I’ll just mention this briefly, you might have known about it or maybe not but, and this was total coincidence but it also was instrumental in helping my career along. When the tour was over we noticed in DownBeat that it was an international jazz competition in Vienna. And it turns out it was the only time this was held, 1966. So several of us made our way from Athens. I think that’s where the tour dropped us off, to Vienna. I remember my parents showed up, they wanted to see me after the four months, and it looked like it was going to be fun. The judges were Art Farmer, Cannonball Adderley, J.J. Johnson, Ron Carter, Mel Lewis, and Joe Zawinul. It was put together by Friedrich Gulda, a wonderful Viennese pianist. So man it looked like, pretty exciting. And the unusual thing was, and I’ve mentioned this several times, there were maybe 200 young musicians at this thing going through semi-semi finals, semi-finals, and then the finals. So we were there about ten days, maybe twelve days, in a youth hostel. So this is where I met a lot of other young musicians my age. People like — unknown then — we were all teenagers: George Mraz, Miroslav Vitous, Jan Hammer, Claudio Roditi, Joachim © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Kuhn, James Williams, Franco Ambrosetti, Eddie Daniels, and I’m leaving out a lot of people that became famous in Europe. So this was really instrumental in all our development. We got to play together a lot and meet the judges, pal around, and when I moved to New York I didn’t quite finish but I went to NYU for a semester and then I kind of got enveloped into the work scene. It was a lot of work back then and I had met Thad and I mean Mel, and Mel asked me to join his big band, and Ron was calling me for gigs, so it couldn’t have been a better scenario. Miroslav and Mraz came to town shortly thereafter, as did Jan, we played together. So it’s kind of like —
It’s kind of like a fairy tale if you ask me.

Yeah. I have to pinch myself looking back. I’m sure we all felt the same way, it was just perfect timing for that. And lo and behold that was the only time — now there are other festivals in Europe, particularly there’s one in Israel. But that was the only time they did that in Vienna. It was just perfect for all of us.
